svg.title: Same functional correctness, different DAG execution efficiency
svg.desc: Two cost-versus-performance panels for all eighteen model and effort settings on the fixed 1500-task dependency-chain workload with three worker limit. X is API-equivalent generation cost per DAG attempt. Y is generated-code median runtime in milliseconds in the first panel and peak Python allocation in KiB in the second. Hollow points are candidate repetitions, filled points are means of two candidates. All DAG main scores are one hundred. This is generated-code performance, not model latency.
svg.text: Correct DAG code can have different execution efficiency
Fixed workload: 1,500-task dependency chain; three worker limit
r2: individual attempts; filled effort shapes are pair means
Peak Python allocation (KiB) - lower is better
Sol 6.1 Low -> Ultra: 2.11x generation cost; all four main grades are 100/100.
Runtime: 77.3 -> 52.3 ms. Peak Python allocation: 781.3 -> 704.7 KiB.
Runtime uses the median of three timings per candidate, then the mean of two candidate medians.
Memory is tracemalloc peak Python allocation, not total process memory. One workload on one machine.
Both repeated candidates support the runtime direction; no general performance ranking follows from this task.
